Airflow retries, explained with real failures

By Noor Haldar · 2026-08-14

Retries look simple: set retries=3 and move on. In production they interact with timeouts, pools, sensors and non-idempotent tasks in ways the documentation only hints at. Here are three failures I have debugged, and what changed afterwards.

1. Retries with no delay hammer a struggling API

A task with retries=5 and the default delay retried against a rate-limited API while it was recovering, and kept it down for longer. Exponential backoff with retry_exponential_backoff=True and a max_retry_delay fixed it.

2. A retried task that was not idempotent

The task inserted rows, failed on the last step, and inserted them again on retry. The fix was to make the write idempotent with a merge on a natural key, not to remove the retries.

3. Sensors, timeouts and retries multiplying

A sensor with a long timeout and three retries held a worker slot for hours. Reschedule mode and a single, explicit timeout solved it.

What I check now

  • Every task with retries has a delay, and backoff when it calls an external service.
  • Every retried task is idempotent.
  • Sensors use reschedule mode and one timeout.

pipeline-lint flags the first and third automatically.
